reference.ticks_note: x_m/y_m/z_m/pitch_deg are config/camera.json's mount, and both are MEASURED, not fitted (2026-09-12): the tape reads floor to tilt axis 1.134 m (axis_z_m, a documented number nothing reads) and lens to axis 0.086 m up, 0.025 m forward, which is the pivot block below; the pitch comes from the encoder and four still frames of one room — head level by eye the tilt servo reads 2068 ticks and the picture is 1.0 deg down (+-1.5), and this reference sits 243 ticks further down, so 23.8 deg. The tilt scale those frames verify is the plain 360/4096 per tick (1.07 true degrees per commanded degree, 1.03..1.09 over every variant): pepin.neck.RAD_PER_TICK needs no correction and there is no scale field here (scratch/neck_tilt_scale.txt). The 26.0 deg / 1.23 m these replace came from the lidar-beam fit of 2026-09-10 (scratch/depth_fit_models.py), which was owed a repeat anyway. pan_ticks and tilt_ticks are what the two encoders read at that pose: 2021 / 2311, read 2026-09-11 through the base server with the head untouched since the mount was measured (50 reads, min = max, scratch/neck_ticks_probe.py). Were they null, while they are null the model ignores the encoders and answers the static mount for every reading (pepin.neck.joint_angles), so /neck/state and the neck_tf transform stand still while the head moves. To fill them, leave the head at rest, deploy the base server that answers the neck command (board/README.md) and ask it on its JSON-lines port: { printf '{"cmd":"neck"}\n'; sleep 2; } | nc 10.0.0.187 3336 | grep -m1 '"type":"neck"' — the reply carries pan_ticks and tilt_ticks (the port also broadcasts state lines, hence the grep). scratch/neck_ticks_probe.py --host 10.0.0.187 --n 50 does the same 50 times and prints median/min/max and what the read costs the bus.
reference.signs_note: pan_sign and tilt_sign say which way an increasing tick count turns the camera. VERIFIED 2026-09-11 by hand with the servos unpowered, watching /neck/state (scratch/neck_signs.csv): the head pushed down took head_tilt from 26 to 103 deg (tilt_sign +1 holds), the head turned to the robot's left took neck_pan from 0 to -124 deg with pan_sign +1, hence pan_sign -1. The check, for a re-assembled neck, in daylight and after the reference ticks are filled in: ros/feature.sh neck on, watch ros2 topic echo /neck/state (or the node's report line), and move the head BY HAND — the base server torques the wheels only (pepin.base.DiffDriveBase.enable), so the neck servos are free to push. Tilting the head down, the picture tilting down with it, must make head_tilt GROW; if it shrinks, tilt_sign is -1. Panning the head to the robot's left (+y of base_link) must make neck_pan GROW; if it shrinks, pan_sign is -1. Then set signs_verified true. The powered version of the same check is scripts/jog.py neck --id 10 --delta 100, which needs the servo bus on the USB of the machine running it and pepin-base stopped on the board (board/README.md) — on the assembled robot the hand check is the cheap one.
reference.pivot_note: the lever arms below: camera_from_tilt_* are the tape of 2026-09-12 (the lens sits 0.086 m above the tilt axis and 0.025 m in front of it, in the head's own frame), so the camera now swings on a real arm as the head tilts instead of turning about its own point. tilt_from_pan_* are still zero and still unmeasured: the pan never moved in any of the measurements, so nothing constrains them. Measure with a ruler, neck straight: pan axis to tilt axis, forward and up.
reference.pan_note: pan_ticks 1993, not the 2021 read on 2026-09-12: with 2021 the camera's heading sat 2.5 deg left of the lidar's — depth_fusion's align stage turned every frame by a signed median of -2.5 deg (three sessions, 2026-09-13), the camera's pose measurements read 2 deg under the tracker's yaw, and the turn lag of the drives was +2.6 deg. pan_sign -1 and 360/4096 deg per tick make that 28 ticks; the head does not move, the number says where 'straight ahead' really is. MEASURED 2026-09-15 for the first time, and the answer is DO NOT SET IT YET (scratch/fan_yaw_offset.py, pepin.extrinsics): matching the camera's obstacle fan against the lidar's over yaw shifts of -8..+8 deg gives a repeatable minimum WITHIN a run (+5.9, +6.0, +6.0 deg; +5.3, +5.4, +5.8 in the next run, three 10 s windows each) but a shallow one — the score climbs only 0.3..1.0 cm per degree away from it, and the run-to-run spread is 0.6 deg. Two things must be fixed before that number means the neck. First, /depth_scan carries no pan at all: depth_stream folds the depth onto the floor as if the head looked along the cart's x whatever the encoders say (_as_scan, counted in its report line as "head panned N frames (projected as if not)"), so the shift measures the camera's true heading, not the reference's error, and the two differ by whatever /neck/state believes (-2.46 deg while this was measured — the head sits at 2021 ticks, the OLD reference, never re-homed after the 28-tick move). Second, the camera's ranges read 0.573 of the lidar's at the same bearings with a -0.4 %/deg slope across the fan; under a range bias that big and that bearing-dependent a yaw and a scale are not separable, which is exactly why the minimum is shallow. Taken at face value the numbers would say pan error +7.86 deg and PROPOSE 1993 -> 2082 ticks; that proposal is NOT to be applied. Redo after the depth law reads near 1.00 against the lidar and depth_stream's scan projection honours the pan: docker cp scratch/fan_yaw_offset.py pepin-vslam:/tmp/ && docker exec pepin-vslam /pepin_entrypoint.sh timeout -s KILL 60 python3 /tmp/fan_yaw_offset.py. To apply a reference once one is believed: set pan_ticks here, restart the neck node, and check with ros/neck.sh read that the head at rest reads 0.0 deg. CHECKED 2026-09-15 by a second pass, and the refusal stands for a sharper reason than the one above. The probe reproduces (+5.8, +5.8, +5.9 deg over three 10 s windows, median +5.80, ratio 0.578, slope -0.0038..-0.0040/deg, /neck/state believing -2.46 deg, every window printing 'flat'), and the proposal it prints moved 2082 -> 2087 ticks between two runs minutes apart with the head untouched. The sign chain is NOT the problem: the estimator returns +delta for a camera really turned delta counter-clockwise, and the reference it proposes makes pepin.neck.joint_angles answer the measured heading at the ticks the head sits at (both are tests now). The problem is the bearing-dependent range bias, and it is bigger than 'not separable': with the camera NOT turned by a single degree, a camera/lidar ratio sliding 0.002 per degree across the fan moves the minimum by about 6 deg AND the minimum passes the sharpness test - the live slope is twice that, and a real +3 deg turn under it reads back as -8 deg (scratch/fan_yaw_confounds.py). A pure scale is not the confound (scale_free divides it out and answers 0.0); the slope is. So the +5.8 deg carries no information about the neck at all, and note what it would say if it did: +5.8 deg of true heading at 2021 ticks proposes a reference ABOVE 2021, i.e. the 2021 -> 1993 move of 2026-09-13 went the wrong way (the branch the journal named that evening). That is not evidence while the law reads 0.58 of the lidar - it is one more reason to fix the law first and measure after. MEASURED AGAIN ACROSS PITCH 2026-09-15 02:10-02:25 (three head pitches, three 10 s windows each) and the refusal stands a third time, now with a reason that names the fan itself: the shifts are +3.1 deg at 14.1 down, +5.4 at 23.8 (the working pitch) and +3.5 at 33.6, and NO rigid mount can produce that shape. A pan is the same angle at every pitch and a roll is roll * sin(pitch), so both together are MONOTONIC in pitch (pepin.extrinsics.mount_yaw_shift); these rise and fall. The joint least-squares fit (pepin.extrinsics.fit_mount, scratch/fan_mount_fit.py) answers pan +3.42 deg, roll +1.44 deg and leaves 0.99 deg rms - ten times the 0.1 deg the three windows at the working pitch repeat to. The reason the shifts are not a mount's is the fan: k = fan/lidar reads 0.99 at 14.1 deg and 0.58 at 23.8 and 33.6, and no uniform depth-law scale can do that (scratch/fan_floor_leak.py, the real depth_to_scan on a raycast room): above kappa = 1 - 0.15/1.203 = 0.875 the fan is the wall and k = kappa at EVERY pitch, below it the whole floor enters the 0.15-1.30 m band and k collapses to 0.44 at 23.8 and 0.31 at 33.6. k = 0.58 at the working pitch is neither: the fan is part wall, part floor, so at that pitch it is not measuring the room the lidar measures. Lidar beams are in view at all three pitches (past 1.00, 0.71 and 0.49 m), so 'the frame law had nothing to fit on at 33.6' is not the explanation. And the bearing slope finishes it: in a synthetic room a slope of only -0.001/deg, with the camera not turned by one degree, reads back as -5.2 deg, and the live slopes (-0.0040 at 23.8, -0.0082 at 14.1) saturate the +-8 deg search - the artefact is bigger than the whole signal (pepin.extrinsics.slope_artefact, a test now). The pan reference stays 1993 - not because 1993 is right (two of the three signals behind the 2021 -> 1993 move of 2026-09-13 come through this same camera fan and inherit its defect) but because nothing measured since carries information about it. The measurement that will settle it does not use ranges at all: a vertical edge's BEARING in the picture (u -> atan((cx - u)/fx), the calibrated intrinsics alone) against the same edge's bearing in the lidar. No depth law enters that number. Until then: leave the reference, and no roll term in config/camera.json - the +1.44 deg the fit offers is fitted to an artefact, and a roll shows in a single frame as a tilted horizon long before it shows in a fan.
